references.title: Identification of autosomal recessive novel genes and retinal phenotypes in members of the solute carrier (SLC) superfamily

comments: a screen of 433 solute carrier genes in a large cohort of Israeli patients with inherited retinal diseases revealed different homozygous variants in SLC66A1 in two consanguineous families with RP

references.title: Non-syndromic retinal dystrophy associated with biallelic variation of SUMF1 and reduced leukocyte sulfatase activity

comments: The SUMF1 gene encodes an enzyme (FGE) required for posttranslational modification and catalytic activation of the family of sulfatase enzymes. In general, mutations in the SUMF1 gene cause multiple sulfatase deficiency (MSD), a rare lysosomal storage disorder. Several patients with an attenuated MSD disease phenotype resulting from biallelic SUMF1 variants, including an adult individual with non-syndromic retinal dystrophy, have also been identified.

references.title: Expanding the phenotype of THRB: a range of macular dystrophies as the major clinical manifestations in patients with a dominant splicing variant

comments: recurrent splice site variant in three unrelated Spanish families with autosomal dominant cone-dominated IRDs. Mutations in THRB previously found in dominant and recessive thyroid hormone resistance syndrome beta (RTHß) but no splicing variants reported for those diseases. Numerous studies in model organisms have established a role for TRß2,one of two THRB isoforms, during cone subtype specification.

references.title: CLEC3B is a novel causative gene for macular-retinal dystrophy

comments: one pathogenic variant (A180D) identified in 5 large Japanese families; gene encodes a plasminogen kringle-4 binding protein; overexpression of the A180D Clec3b variant in mouse retina appeared to mimic features of  the human phenotype

references.title: Mutated CCDC51 Coding for a Mitochondrial Protein, MITOK Is a Candidate Gene Defect for Autosomal Recessive Rod-Cone Dystrophy

comments: Homozygous frameshift mutation in a consanguineous family; phenotype of the affected patient was a relatively mild rod-cone dystrophy; CCDC51, alias MITOK, codes for a mitochondrial protein and localizes in the inner segments of rod and cone photoreceptors

references.title: Biallelic CLCN2 mutations cause retinal degeneration by impairing retinal pigment epithelium phagocytosis and chloride channel function

comments: Patient with homozygous nonsense CLCN2 mutation presented with leukodystrophy and was later diagnosed with severe bilateral retinal degeneration with loss of photoreceptors and RPE; patient iPSC-derived RPE cells carrying the CLCN2 mutation exhibited dysfunctional ClC-2 chloride channels and outer segment phagocytosis

disease: recessive cone-rod or macular dystrophy, late onset

references.title: XXYLT1 and Mendelian Retinal Dystrophy

comments: GWAS analysis of FinnGen samples identified possible IRD loci; followup in smaller IRD cohorts from Finland and the UK identified a homozygous pathogenic splice-site variant in the XXYLTI gene that resulted in a cone-rod phenotype in multiple families and a homozygous amino acid substitution that led to a macular dystrophy phenotype.

references.title: Biallelic variants in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis pathway genes cause a retinitis pigmentosa phenotype

comments: distinct biallelic mutations in the COQ2 gene were found in three families with RP alone, or RP and renal disease; the families were part of a cohort of patients with inherited retinal diseases screened for genes involved in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis

disease: recessive complete congenital stationary night blindness

references.title: EGFLAM Pathogenic Variants and Congenital Stationary Night Blindness

comments: two different homozygous LOF variants in EGFLAM were identified in two families with typical cCSNB including high myopia; the EGFLAM protein interacts with GPR179, located on the ON-bipolar cell membrane, and is important for ON-bipolar cell signaling in the retina

references.title: CEP162 deficiency causes human retinal degeneration and reveals a dual role in ciliogenesis and neurogenesis

comments: two unrelated Moroccan families with late onset RP share the same homozygous truncating mutation; truncated protein escapes nonsense-mediated decay and fails to correctly localize to the basal body in primary and photoreceptor cilia and results in delayed formation of dysmorphic cilia

references.title: TBC1D32 variants disrupt retinal ciliogenesis and cause retinitis pigmentosa

comments: four patients presenting with RP from three unrelated families and an additional 4th European family, most patients shared abnormal visibility of large choroidal vessels in the peripheral retina, suggesting RPE loss; recessive loss-of-function TBC1D32 variants reported as responsible for oral-facial-digital (OFD) syndrome type IX, a ciliopathy; in a Xenopus model, tbc1d32 is expressed in retinal progenitors, developing photoreceptors, and RPE cells, consistent with a putative role in retinogenesis.

references.title: Bi-allelic variants in three genes encoding distinct subunits of the vesicular AP-5 complex cause hereditary macular dystrophy

comments: pathogenic mutations in three different subunits (AP5Z1, AP5M1, AP5B1) of the vesicular fifth adaptor protein (AP-5) complex identified in 22 individuals with recessive MD from 19 unrelated families; all subjects had progressive MD with average onset during the 5th decade of life; retinal phenotype consistent across all genotypes/genes; half of affected individuals exhibited extraocular features of variable severity but not consistent; the AP-5 complex is involved in maintaining cellular homeostasis; disruption impairs lysosomal function and endosome trafficking, leading to a previously unrecognized type of lysosomal storage disease (LSD); immunostaining of RPE cells showed punctate labeling of all three proteins on the apical side of the cell and co-localization with markers of late endosomes and the Golgi

references.title: Impaired complex I repair causes recessive Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy

comments: mutations in this nuclear-encoded gene, including a common founder, account for cases of LHON which are not mitochondrial in origin; hallmarks of mtLHON were recapitulated, including incomplete penetrance, male predominance, and significant idebenone responsivity; DNAJC30 is a chaperone protein needed for the efficient exchange of complex I subunits exposed to reactive oxygen species and integral to a mitochondrial complex I repair mechanism

disease: recessive retinitis pigmentosa with macular degeneration

references.title: Identification of autosomal recessive novel genes and retinal phenotypes in members of the solute carrier (SLC) superfamily

comments: a screen of 433 solute carrier genes in a large cohort of Israeli patients with inherited retinal diseases revealed a homozygous variant in SLC37A3 in one consanguineous family with RP and macular degeneration

references.title: Novel Compound Heterozygous Variations in MPDZ Gene Caused Isolated Bilateral Macular Coloboma in a Chinese Family

comments: rdd locus in chickens (retinal dysplasia and degeneration) mapped to candidate gene mpdz which interacts with CRB1. MPDZ variants have been described in cases of recessive congenital hydrocephalus with varying ophthalmologic manifestations. Rare cases of macular coloboma without systemic abnormalities reported. Knockdown of MPDZ in zebrafish caused a decrease in the ellipsoid zone, destruction of the outer limiting membrane, and subsequent RPE degeneration.

references.title: Founder Homozygous Nonsense CREB3 Variant and Variable-Onset Retinal Degeneration

comments: A founder homozygous nonsense variant (c.881G>A, p.Trp294*) was identified in 13 patients from 4 unrelated families; individuals had a nonsyndromic IRD of variable severity, as reflected by the age at onset and the retinal phenotype (RP, CRD); a truncated protein was expressed in patient fibroblasts; gene encodes a transcription factor that is a member of the leucine zipper family of DNA binding proteins; protein was observed in all retinal cell types

disease: recessive retinitis pigmentosa with or without mild neurological involvement

references.title: Bi-allelic variants in FSD1L cause retinitis pigmentosa with or without neurological involvement

comments: bi-allelic ultra-rare variants found in six individuals with RP with or without mild neurological features from four unrelated families; recent publication implicates FSDL1 variants in a severe neurodevelopmental phenotype as well; gene is found to be expressed in the retina, particularly in photoreceptors, and the protein localizes to the photoreceptor microtubule axoneme, including the connecting cilium and outer segment

references.title: Variants in NR6A1 cause a novel oculo vertebral renal syndrome

comments: six rare NR6A1 variants in six families affected by uveal coloboma; characterized by colobomatous microphthalmia, missing vertebrae and congenital kidney abnormalities; gene encodes an orphan nuclear receptor which is a member of the nuclear hormone receptor family; knockdown of either or both zebrafish paralogs of NR6A1 results in abnormal eye, kidney, and somite development, which was rescued by wild-type but not variant NR6A1 mRNA

references.title: Biallelic variants in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis pathway genes cause a retinitis pigmentosa phenotype

comments: distinct biallelic mutations in the COQ4 gene were found in one family with recessive RP; the family was part of a cohort of patients with inherited retinal diseases screened for genes involved in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis

references.title: WDR34, a candidate gene for non-syndromic rod-cone dystrophy

comments: also called WD repeat-containing protein 34 (WDR34)

references.title: Identification of autosomal recessive novel genes and retinal phenotypes in members of the solute carrier (SLC) superfamily

comments: a screen of 433 solute carrier genes in a large cohort of Israeli patients with inherited retinal diseases revealed homozygous variants in SLC39A2 in four consanguineous family with RP

references.title: Biallelic variants in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis pathway genes cause a retinitis pigmentosa phenotype

comments: distinct biallelic mutations in the PDSS1 gene were found in six families with recessive RP, or RP and hearing impairment

references.title: Pathogenic STX3 variants affecting the retinal and intestinal transcripts cause an early-onset severe retinal dystrophy in microvillus inclusion disease subjects

comments: Biallelic STX3 variants were first reported in individuals with microvillus inclusion disease (MVID); additional studies of patients with a combination of MVID and an early-onset severe retinal dystrophy revealed a different set of causative mutations. Most recently, mutations in the retina-specific isoform, STX3B, were found in patients with the retinal phenotype alone; the two isoforms, STX3A and STX3B, share 8 exons - mutations in these regions cause the syndromic phenotype; mutations in exon 9A, from STX3A, cause only the gastrointestinal phenotype; mutations in exon 9B, from the retinal-specific STX3B, only appear to cause the retinal phenotype;  in rodents, Stx3 localizes to the synaptic boutons of photoreceptors and bipolar cells and to the inner segments of photoreceptors and has been implicated in the trafficking of rhodopsin to the outer segments of rod photoreceptors.

references.title: Bi-allelic variants in three genes encoding distinct subunits of the vesicular AP-5 complex cause hereditary macular dystrophy

comments: pathogenic mutations in three different subunits (AP5Z1, AP5M1, AP5B1) of the vesicular fifth adaptor protein (AP-5) complex identified in 22 individuals with recessive MD from 19 unrelated families; all subjects had progressive MD with average onset during the 5th decade of life; retinal phenotype consistent across all genotypes/genes; half of affected individuals exhibited extraocular features of variable severity but not consistent; the AP-5 complex is involved in maintaining cellular homeostasis; disruption impairs lysosomal function and endosome trafficking, leading to a previously unrecognized type of lysosomal storage disease (LSD); immunostaining of RPE cells showed punctate labeling of all three proteins on the apical side of the cell and co-localization with markers of late endosomes and the Golgi

references.title: Loss-of-function variants in SAXO6, encoding a microtubule inner protein of photoreceptor cilia, cause a late-onset retinal dystrophy

comments: bi-allelic combinations of six predicted null variants in MDM1 (now renamed SAXO6) were identified in six subjects from five families with late-onset RP or CRD; protein experimentally shown to be a ciliary microtubule inner protein (MIP); localizes throughout the axonemes of motile and non-motile cilia

references.title: De novo and inherited dominant variants in U4 and U6 snRNA genes cause retinitis pigmentosa

comments: both inherited and de novo variants in RNU4-2 and four paralogs of RNU6, encoding the U4 and U6 snRNAs, found as the molecular cause of adRP in 153 individuals across 67 families. All identified variants cluster within the U4/U6 duplex, in a region that binds directly to PRPF31 and PRPF3 and indirectly to PRPF6 and PRPF816,17. These variants increase the association of U4 and U6 snRNAs with the splicing factors SART3 and PRPF31, suggesting impaired snRNP biogenesis.

references.title: Biallelic variants in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis pathway genes cause a retinitis pigmentosa phenotype

comments: distinct biallelic mutations in the COQ5 gene were found in two families with recessive RP; the families were part of a cohort of patients with inherited retinal diseases screened for genes involved in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis

references.title: Mutations in VWA8 cause autosomal-dominant retinitis pigmentosa via aberrant mitophagy activation

comments: two variants, one LOF, on the same allele segregate in a single large 4-generation Chinese family, encodes a mitochondrial matrix-targeted protein, phenotypes of zebrafish with VWA8 knockdown are similar to patient phenotype

comments: across three studies, 6 UBAP1L loss-of-function variants identified in 18 IRD families; gene expressed in rod and cone photoreceptors of zebrafish; rods, cones, and RPE in humans; mouse model with C-terminal truncation did not show retinal degeneration up to15 months of age; function of UBAP1L protein unknown but believed to bind ubiquitin

references.title: A comprehensive WGS-based pipeline for the identification of new candidate genes in inherited retinal dystrophies.

comments: rare cause of disease; homozygous missense variant found in a consanguineous family from Spain; CFAP20 has  been detected in the primary cilium-derived photosensory rod outer segments of mouse retina; knockdown experiments in zebrafish revealed a phenotype consistent with ciliary dysfunction

disease: dominant chorioretinal coloboma and microthalmia with sensorineural hearing loss

references.title: A Novel De Novo Missense Variant in Netrin-1 (NTN1) Associated With Chorioretinal Coloboma, Sensorineural Hearing Loss and Polydactyly

comments: Netrin-1 was previously identified as a mediator of optic fissure closure and shown to cause ocular coloboma when knocked out in mouse and zebrafish; single human patient identified with a heterozygous de novo missense variant with phenotype including unilateral left microcornea, left esotropia and left chorioretinal coloboma. The patient also had bilateral SNHL and polydactyly; dominant mutations in a different part of the protein cause mirror movements-4 (MRMV4)

disease: biallelic pathogenic variants identified in 15 individuals from 11 unrelated families, all affected by  a recessive IRD;  patients typically show a late-onset phenotype with symptoms characteristic to RCD which advances to a unique and distinctive retinal phenotype of patchy perifoveal chorioretinal atrophy; phenotypes of patients with the same combination of pathogenic variants also reported to be quite different, with RP characteristics and macular sparing; protein of unknown function with ubiquitous expression, does not appear to be ciliary.

references.title: Biallelic null variants in C19orf44 cause a unique late-onset retinal dystrophy phenotype characterized by patchy perifoveal chorioretinal atrophy.
Bi-allelic variants in COQ8B, a gene involved in the biosynthesis of coenzyme Q10, lead to non-syndromic retinitis pigmentosa

comments: four families with five individuals with potentially disease-causing bi-allelic variants in COQ8B; wide range in age-of-onset and severity, though mostly mild; variants in COQ8B are a known cause of steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) but no renal symptoms were found in this group of arRP patients; COQ8B is predicted to function as a kinase participating in CoQ biosynthesis, exhibiting ATPase activity in the presence of CoQ intermediates.

references.title: Nuclear DNA Mutation Causing a Phenotypic Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy Plus

comments: first known case of LHON associated with a pathogenic mutation of a nuclear gene that encodes a mitochondrial complex I assembly factor; single patient with acute visual loss and dystonia; whole mtDNA genome sequencing excluded the three primary LHON mutations; two compound heterozygous variants identified in NDUFAF5;  previously, biallelic mutations in NDUFAF5 identified in patients with mitochondrial complex I deficiency nuclear type 16 (MC1DN16)

disease: recessive severe intellectual disability (ID) and retinitis pigmentosa

references.title: A loss of function variant in AGPAT3 underlies intellectual disability and retinitis pigmentosa (IDRP) syndrome
Dominant mutations in MIEF1 affect mitochondrial dynamics and cause a singular late onset optic neuropathy

comments: heterozygous missense mutations in MIEF1 found in two women with late-onset optic atrophy

references.title: Identification of IDH3G, encoding the gamma subunit of mitochondrial isocitrate dehydrogenase, as a novel candidate gene for X-linked retinitis pigmentosa

comments: four rare single nucleotide variants as well as a complete gene deletion in five male probands with nonsyndromic RP; IDH3G encodes the gamma subunit of mitochondrial isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH3), an enzyme involved in the citric acid cycle, expressed in the inner segments of photoreceptors. Variants in IDH3A and IDH3B , encoding the other subunits of IDH3, have already been associated with nonsyndromic autosomal recessive RP; location on the X chromosome is in the RP34 region
